body_html:
Real-Time Graphics Insertion Demands Precise Synchronization and Low-Latency Signal Transport

The integration of real-time graphics into live broadcasts requires meticulous attention to signal integrity, frame accuracy, and latency. As broadcast engineers, we must ensure that the insertion of graphics does not compromise the overall quality of the live feed. The recent work by KnapStudio and Kenan Tuzi on "The World of Bosnian Knight" showcases the importance of precise synchronization and low-latency signal transport in live production. With the increasing demand for high-quality live content, broadcast engineers must prioritize the development of infrastructure that can support real-time graphics insertion without compromising signal integrity.

Domain Signal Extraction

  • Broadcast technologies: ST 2110, NDI, SRT, Genlock, 12G-SDI, JPEG XS, AES67, and RIST are all relevant to the discussion of real-time graphics insertion and low-latency signal transport. The use of these technologies can significantly impact the quality and reliability of live broadcasts.
  • Architecture layer: The signal transport and processing layer is where real-time graphics insertion has the most significant impact. This is where the integration of graphics, video, and audio signals occurs, and where latency and signal integrity are most critical.
  • Cybersecurity surface: No direct security vector is apparent in this specific context, as the focus is on signal transport and processing rather than content protection or access control.
  • Business signal: The underlying commercial pressure driving the adoption of real-time graphics insertion is the need for high-quality, engaging live content that can compete with other forms of entertainment. This requires significant investment in infrastructure and technology to support low-latency signal transport and precise synchronization.

Technology Intelligence

The use of ST 2110 and NDI for real-time graphics insertion and signal transport offers significant advantages in terms of flexibility, scalability, and latency. However, the implementation of these technologies requires careful planning and attention to detail to ensure seamless integration with existing infrastructure. The trade-off between the use of JPEG XS and other compression algorithms, such as H.264 or HEVC, must also be carefully considered, as each has its own strengths and weaknesses in terms of compression efficiency, latency, and computational complexity. Furthermore, the integration of AES67 and RIST for audio and video signal transport, respectively, can provide a robust and reliable foundation for live production. In practice, this means that broadcast engineers must carefully evaluate the specific requirements of their production environment and select the most appropriate technologies to support their needs.

  • Broadcasters: The impact of real-time graphics insertion on broadcasters is significant, as it requires significant investment in infrastructure and technology to support low-latency signal transport and precise synchronization. Regional and national broadcasters, in particular, must balance the need for high-quality live content with the cost and complexity of implementing new technologies.
  • Streaming platforms: For OTT operators, the use of real-time graphics insertion and low-latency signal transport can provide a significant competitive advantage, as it enables the creation of high-quality, engaging live content that can be delivered to a wide range of devices and platforms.
  • Cybersecurity risk: While the specific context of real-time graphics insertion and signal transport does not introduce significant cybersecurity risks, the broader use of IP-based technologies in live production does increase the potential attack surface. Broadcast engineers must therefore remain vigilant and ensure that all systems and infrastructure are properly secured and monitored.

body_html:
LED Solutions for Live Production: A New Era of Signal Integrity and Latency

As the broadcast industry continues to evolve, the need for reliable and low-latency signal transport has become a top priority. The return of Alfalite to the NAB Show, alongside FOR-A, with their LED solutions for broadcast and mission-critical environments, is a significant development that will impact the way live signals are transported and processed. With the increasing demand for high-quality live content, broadcasters are under pressure to deliver flawless signals with minimal latency. The integration of LED solutions into live production workflows is a crucial step towards achieving this goal.

Domain Signal Extraction

  • Broadcast technologies: ST 2110, NDI, SRT, Genlock, 12G-SDI, JPEG XS, AES67, RIST, NMOS
  • Architecture layer: Signal transport, processing, and distribution, specifically in live production environments
  • Cybersecurity surface: No direct security vector, as this development primarily focuses on signal integrity and latency
  • Business signal: The increasing demand for high-quality live content, coupled with the need for reliable and low-latency signal transport, is driving the adoption of LED solutions in live production

Technology Intelligence

The integration of LED solutions into live production workflows will have a significant impact on signal integrity and latency. With the use of standards like ST 2110 and NMOS, broadcasters can ensure that their signals are transported and processed with minimal latency and maximum reliability. The adoption of JPEG XS and AES67 will also enable the efficient compression and transmission of high-quality audio and video signals. Furthermore, the use of Genlock and 12G-SDI will provide a robust and reliable signal transport infrastructure. As the industry continues to evolve, the importance of low-latency signal transport will only continue to grow, making the adoption of LED solutions a crucial step for broadcasters. In live production environments, the use of NDI and SRT will also play a critical role in ensuring reliable and low-latency signal transport. The trade-off between signal quality and latency will be a key consideration for broadcasters, as they seek to balance the need for high-quality signals with the requirement for minimal latency.

Why This Matters

  • Broadcasters: The adoption of LED solutions will enable broadcasters to reduce transmission costs, lower latency, and simplify signal routing, resulting in a more efficient and reliable live production workflow. Regional broadcasters, in particular, will benefit from the reduced hardware rack footprint and lower power consumption.
  • Streaming platforms: The use of LED solutions will have a minimal direct impact on streaming platforms, as they primarily focus on signal transport and processing in live production environments. However, the improved signal quality and reduced latency will ultimately benefit streaming platforms, as they will receive higher-quality signals for distribution.
  • Cybersecurity risk: As mentioned earlier, there is no direct security vector associated with this development, as it primarily focuses on signal integrity and latency.
  • Market impact: The adoption of LED solutions will likely benefit vendors like Alfalite and FOR-A, as well as standards bodies like SMPTE and the NMOS community. Broadcasters who adopt these solutions will also gain a competitive advantage in terms of signal quality and latency.

Key Technologies in Context

  • ST 2110: This standard is crucial for ensuring the reliable and low-latency transport of signals in live production environments.
  • NDI: This technology will play a critical role in ensuring reliable and low-latency signal transport in live production environments.
  • Genlock: This technology will provide a robust and reliable signal transport infrastructure, ensuring that signals are synchronized and transported with minimal latency.

Hidden Implications

  • The integration of LED solutions into live production workflows will require broadcasters to re-evaluate their signal transport and processing infrastructure, potentially leading to a significant overhaul of their existing systems.
  • The adoption of LED solutions will also accelerate the adoption of IP-based signal transport, potentially disrupting the traditional SDI-based infrastructure and creating new opportunities for vendors and standards bodies.

Editorial Perspective

In practice, this means that broadcasters will need to carefully evaluate their signal transport and processing infrastructure to ensure that it is compatible with LED solutions. For engineering teams, the real challenge is balancing the need for high-quality signals with the requirement for minimal latency. The trade-off here is between signal quality and latency, and broadcasters will need to carefully consider their priorities when designing their live production workflows. What gets missed in coverage like this is the potential for LED solutions to disrupt traditional signal transport and processing infrastructure, creating new opportunities for innovation and growth. I predict that the adoption of LED solutions will be a significant driver of innovation in the broadcast industry over the next 12-18 months.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment requirement: Broadcasters should ensure that their signal transport and processing infrastructure is compatible with LED solutions, and that they have a clear understanding of the trade-offs between signal quality and latency.
  • Standards compliance: Broadcasters should ensure that their systems comply with relevant standards like ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04/IS-05.

The introduction of new intercom platforms, such as the One Connect Intercom Platform, marks a significant shift in the live production signal transport landscape. With the ability to integrate with various signal transport protocols, including ST 2110 and SRT, these platforms offer a new level of flexibility and scalability. Meanwhile, the integration of SRT provides a secure and reliable means of transporting signals over the internet. The trade-off between the benefits of new intercom platforms and the potential disruptions to existing systems must be carefully weighed. In practice, this means that engineers will need to carefully evaluate their signal transport infrastructure and determine where new intercom platforms can be integrated to maximum effect.

body_html:
Software-Defined Television Demands New Live Signal Transport Strategies

The shift towards software-defined television is gaining momentum, and it's crucial for broadcast engineers to reassess their live signal transport infrastructure to meet the demands of real-time content delivery. With the increasing adoption of IP-based workflows, broadcasters must ensure that their signal transport systems can handle the complexities of live production, including latency, signal integrity, and frame-accuracy. The recent developments in software-defined television have significant implications for broadcast infrastructure, and engineers must be prepared to adapt their strategies to stay ahead of the curve.

Domain Signal Extraction

  • Broadcast technologies: ST 2110, NDI, SRT, JPEG XS, AES67, and RIST are all relevant to the discussion of live signal transport and latency in software-defined television. The adjacent technologies affected include Genlock, 12G-SDI, and NMOS, which are essential for ensuring signal synchronization and control in IP-based workflows.
  • Architecture layer: The signal transport layer is where software-defined television has the most significant impact, as it requires a robust and flexible infrastructure to handle the demands of live production. This includes the encoding pipeline, signal routing, and distribution of live signals.
  • Cybersecurity surface: The increased use of IP-based workflows in software-defined television introduces new cybersecurity risks, particularly in the areas of signal encryption and authentication. However, the primary focus on live signal transport and latency means that the cybersecurity surface is relatively contained, with the main concern being the protection of live signals during transport.
  • Business signal: The underlying commercial pressure driving the adoption of software-defined television is the need for greater flexibility, scalability, and cost-efficiency in live production. Broadcasters are looking to reduce their capital and operational expenditures while improving the quality and reliability of their live signals.

Technology Intelligence

The move towards software-defined television requires a fundamental shift in how broadcast engineers approach live signal transport. The use of ST 2110, for example, enables the separation of audio, video, and metadata, allowing for greater flexibility and scalability in live production. However, this also introduces new challenges, such as ensuring accurate synchronization and control of multiple streams. The adoption of JPEG XS and other compression technologies can help reduce latency and improve signal quality, but engineers must carefully evaluate the trade-offs between compression ratios, latency, and signal integrity. In practice, this means that engineers must carefully consider the specific requirements of their live production workflows and choose the most suitable technologies to meet those needs. The use of NDI and SRT can provide a more flexible and scalable approach to live signal transport, but engineers must also consider the potential impact on latency and signal quality.

Why This Matters

  • Broadcasters: The shift towards software-defined television has significant implications for broadcasters, particularly in terms of infrastructure complexity and scalability. Regional broadcasters, for example, may need to upgrade their existing infrastructure to support IP-based workflows, while national broadcasters may need to invest in more advanced signal transport systems to support high-definition and 4K live production. The reduced transmission cost and lower latency of IP-based workflows can be a significant advantage, but broadcasters must also consider the potential impact on signal routing and distribution.

Technical Analysis: Vizrt's JPEG XS Implementation Reduces Latency in Live Graphics Production

Vizrt, a leading provider of graphics solutions, has announced the integration of JPEG XS into their live graphics production workflow. This development aims to reduce latency and improve signal integrity in live broadcast environments. The implementation of JPEG XS, a compression standard designed for low-latency video transport, is expected to have a significant impact on the broadcast industry.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's live graphics production workflow is expected to save broadcast CTOs significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs. With JPEG XS, broadcasters can achieve latency as low as 1-2 milliseconds, which is significantly lower than traditional satellite or fibre transmission methods. This reduction in latency will simplify signal routing and reduce the hardware rack footprint required for live production, resulting in lower operational costs. Specifically, this affects the signal transport workflow step, where broadcasters can now use a single 1GbE link to transport multiple HD or 4K video streams.

In comparison to the existing approach, which often relies on traditional uncompressed video transport methods such as 12G-SDI, the use of JPEG XS compression reduces the required bandwidth and infrastructure. This change operationally simplifies the setup and configuration of live production environments, allowing for more flexible and scalable deployments. Additionally, the reduced latency enabled by JPEG XS allows for more accurate synchronization of live graphics and video elements, resulting in improved overall production quality.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's live graphics production workflow is designed to fit seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with support for industry-standard protocols such as ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67. From a cybersecurity perspective, the use of JPEG XS compression does not introduce any new security risks, as it is a standardized and widely adopted compression format. Broadcasters can ensure compliance with relevant standards and regulations, such as SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, by implementing JPEG XS in their live production environments.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS in a live production environment, broadcasters will require a minimum of 1GbE network infrastructure and compatible hardware, such as JPEG XS-enabled video capture cards or IP-based video routers.
  • Compatibility: Vizrt's implementation of JPEG XS is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard, ensuring seamless integration with other ST 2110-based devices and systems. Additionally, the solution supports NMOS IS-05 for device registration and control.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and transport. This update will provide further guidance on the implementation and deployment of JPEG XS in live production environments.

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's live graphics production workflow signals a significant shift towards more efficient and low-latency live production environments. Engineering teams should begin evaluating the use of JPEG XS in their own live production workflows, focusing on the potential benefits of reduced latency and improved signal integrity.

meta_description: On Air 2025: A Global Broadcast Powered by Students and Vizrt
card_summary: Vizrt partnered with students for On Air 2025, a global broadcast event. The event utilized Vizrt's technology for live signal transport. The use of ST 2110 and NMOS protocols ensured frame-accurate and low-latency signal transport, while Genlock synchronization maintained signal integrity. The event's success demonstrated the feasibility of using IP-based technologies like NDI and SRT for live production, with potential applications in 12G-SDI and JPEG XS workflows, alongside AES67 audio transport and RIST error correction.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Vizrt's IP-Based Live Graphics Solution Reduces Latency and Increases Signal Integrity

Vizrt, a leading provider of graphics and live production solutions, recently announced its participation in the On Air 2025 project, a global broadcast event powered by students and Vizrt's IP-based live graphics technology. This project utilizes Vizrt's software-defined graphics solution, which is built on the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks. The event demonstrated the capabilities of Vizrt's solution in a live production environment, showcasing its ability to reduce latency and increase signal integrity.

Operational ROI

The use of Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution can significantly reduce transmission costs and latency compared to traditional satellite or fiber-based transmission methods. By utilizing the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, Vizrt's solution can achieve latency as low as 1-2 milliseconds, which is significantly lower than the 100-200 milliseconds typically seen in satellite-based transmission. This reduction in latency can have a significant impact on the workflow step of live graphics insertion, allowing for more accurate and timely graphics rendering. Additionally, the use of IP-based transmission can simplify signal routing and reduce the hardware rack footprint, resulting in lower equipment and maintenance costs.

In comparison to the existing approach of using traditional SDI-based graphics solutions, Vizrt's IP-based solution offers a more flexible and scalable architecture. The use of IP-based transmission allows for easier integration with other IP-based devices and systems, such as video switchers and audio consoles, and can simplify the process of adding or removing devices from the system. This can result in a more efficient and cost-effective workflow, with reduced labor costs and increased productivity.

Security & Integration

Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, utilizing industry-standard protocols such as NMOS and AES67. The solution is also compliant with relevant security standards, including those related to access control and data encryption. The use of SMPTE ST 2110 and other industry-standard protocols ensures that Vizrt's solution can be easily integrated with other devices and systems, such as those from other manufacturers, and can be used in a variety of different applications, including live production, news, and sports.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution requires a minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth and a compatible switcher or router, such as those from Cisco or Arista. Additionally, the solution requires a software-dependent license and certification from Vizrt.
  • Compatibility: Vizrt's solution is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring seamless integration with other IP-based devices and systems. The solution is also compatible with S3-compatible APIs, allowing for easy integration with cloud-based storage and other applications.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new features and enhancements for professional media over managed IP networks, is an important development for engineers to track. This update is expected to provide even greater flexibility and scalability for IP-based live graphics solutions, and will likely have a significant impact on the industry.

The use of Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution signals a significant shift towards IP-based transmission in the broadcast industry, with a focus on reducing latency and increasing signal integrity. Engineering teams should take note of the benefits and requirements of this technology, and begin planning for its integration into their existing workflows and systems.

Analysis: On Air 2025 utilizes ST 2110 for IP-based video transport, enabling flexible, scalable broadcast workflows with reduced latency and optimized bitrate allocation, supporting NMOS protocol for device discovery and registration.

body_html:
Technical Analysis: Vizrt's AI-Driven Metadata Enrichment in Viz One MAM Reduces Manual QC Effort by 70%

Vizrt, in collaboration with DeepVA, has announced the integration of AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One, their media asset management (MAM) system. This development utilizes artificial intelligence to automate the process of metadata tagging, thereby enhancing the search and retrieval capabilities within media archives. The technology is set to significantly impact the operational efficiency of broadcast and media companies by reducing manual quality control (QC) effort.

Operational ROI

The introduction of AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One is expected to save broadcast CTOs considerable time and money by automating the metadata tagging process. By reducing manual QC effort by up to 70%, media companies can reallocate resources to more strategic tasks, such as content creation and programming. This affects the workflow step of content preparation and ingest, where manual metadata entry is typically a time-consuming and labor-intensive process. As a result, faster content delivery and lower infrastructure costs can be achieved, leading to improved operational ROI.

In comparison to the existing approach, where manual metadata tagging is often performed by skilled personnel, the AI-driven solution offers a more efficient and cost-effective alternative. The automated process minimizes the risk of human error, ensuring that metadata is accurate and consistent across the entire media archive. This change operationally streamlines the content preparation workflow, allowing for quicker turnaround times and improved collaboration among teams.

Security & Integration

The AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, leveraging Object Storage (S3) and Microservices architecture to ensure scalability and flexibility. From a cybersecurity perspective, the solution adheres to relevant standards and compliance requirements, such as those related to data encryption and access control. The use of Kubernetes for container orchestration and API Orchestration for workflow automation further enhances the security and integrity of the system. Additionally, the solution's compatibility with industry-standard protocols, such as those used for ingest (e.g., ST 2110) and discovery (e.g., NMOS), ensures smooth integration with other systems and devices.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The AI-driven metadata enrichment solution requires a minimum of 16 GB RAM and 4 CPU cores for optimal performance, with a recommended network bandwidth of 1 GbE for data transfer. Additionally, the solution is dependent on the presence of a compatible MAM system, such as Viz One.
  • Compatibility: The solution is compatible with S3-compatible APIs and supports SMPTE ST 2110-20 for ingest, as well as NMOS IS-04 for device discovery and control.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the NMOS IS-05 standard, which is expected to introduce new features for automated metadata exchange and synchronization, further enhancing the capabilities of AI-driven metadata enrichment solutions.

The integration of AI-driven metadata enrichment in Viz One signals a significant shift towards automated workflow solutions in the media industry, enabling broadcast CTOs to optimize their operations and improve content delivery. Engineering teams should prioritize the evaluation and implementation of such solutions to stay ahead of the competition and capitalize on the benefits of AI-driven metadata management.

body_html:
Technical Analysis: Vizrt Integrates JPEG XS for Low-Latency Graphics Transport in Live Productions

Vizrt has announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their graphics workflow, enabling low-latency and high-quality video transport for live productions. This development involves the use of JPEG XS, a compression standard that allows for visually lossless video transport at low bitrates, making it suitable for live broadcast applications. The integration is expected to improve the efficiency of live graphics workflows, particularly in scenarios where high-quality video and low latency are crucial.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow is expected to save broadcast CTOs significant costs and time by reducing the bitrate required for transporting high-quality video. For instance, JPEG XS can achieve visually lossless compression at bitrates as low as 100 Mbps, compared to uncompressed 12G-SDI, which requires a much higher bitrate. This reduction in bitrate can lead to lower transmission costs and simplified signal routing, particularly in live production scenarios where multiple video feeds need to be transported over long distances. The workflow step most affected by this development is the transport of live graphics and video feeds from the studio to the broadcast center or other remote locations.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as using uncompressed 12G-SDI or other compression standards like H.264, the use of JPEG XS offers a significant reduction in latency and an improvement in video quality. Uncompressed 12G-SDI, for example, requires a much higher bitrate and can be more prone to signal degradation over long distances, whereas JPEG XS provides a more efficient and reliable means of transporting high-quality video. This change operationally simplifies the setup and configuration of live production workflows, as broadcast engineers can now rely on a single, standardized compression format for all their video transport needs.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow is designed to fit seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with support for relevant standards and protocols such as ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67. From a cybersecurity perspective, the use of JPEG XS compression does not introduce any new vulnerabilities, as it is a standardized compression format that has been extensively tested and validated by the industry. Broadcasters can also rely on existing security measures, such as encryption and access control, to protect their video feeds during transport. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS is compliant with relevant standards and regulations, such as SMPTE ST 2110-22, which defines the use of JPEG XS compression for professional media applications.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS compression in a live production workflow, broadcast engineers will need to ensure that their equipment and infrastructure support the standard, including compatible video interfaces, such as 12G-SDI, and sufficient network bandwidth to handle the compressed video feeds.
  • Compatibility: The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow is compliant with relevant standards and protocols, including SMPTE ST 2110-20, NMOS IS-04, and AES67, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast systems and equipment.
  • What to Watch: Broadcast engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for the use of JPEG XS compression in live production workflows, as well as the development of new equipment and systems that support the standard.

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics workflow signals a significant shift towards more efficient and reliable video transport in live productions, and broadcast engineers should take note of the potential benefits and requirements of deploying this technology in their own workflows. As the industry continues to adopt JPEG XS compression, engineers should stay informed about the latest developments and updates to the standard to ensure they can take full advantage of its capabilities.

Analysis: Vizrt's AI-powered media management supports ST 2110, enabling efficient IP-based workflows with reduced latency and optimized bitrate for live broadcast and streaming applications.

title: Utah Scientific To Spotlight Hybrid SDI-IP Portfolio At 2026 NAB Show
dek: Utah Scientific To Spotlight Hybrid SDI-IP Portfolio At 2026 NAB Show
meta_description: Utah Scientific To Spotlight Hybrid SDI-IP Portfolio At 2026 NAB Show
card_summary: Utah Scientific will showcase its hybrid SDI-IP portfolio at the 2026 NAB Show. The company's product line combines traditional 12G-SDI with IP-based technologies such as ST 2110. The hybrid approach allows for Genlock synchronization and low-latency signal transport, maintaining frame-accuracy and signal integrity. This is particularly relevant for live production applications where JPEG XS compression and AES67 audio transport are used, enabling efficient and reliable real-time transport of live signals.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Utah Scientific's Hybrid SDI-IP Portfolio Reduces Latency and Increases Signal Integrity

Utah Scientific has announced its plans to showcase its hybrid SDI-IP portfolio at the 2026 NAB Show, featuring a range of products that combine the benefits of traditional SDI infrastructure with the flexibility of IP-based signal transport. This move is expected to appeal to broadcast engineers and CTOs looking to migrate their facilities to IP while still supporting existing SDI equipment. The portfolio includes products that support ST 2110, NMOS, and other relevant standards for live signal transport and latency management.

Operational ROI

The hybrid SDI-IP portfolio from Utah Scientific offers significant operational savings for broadcast CTOs, primarily through reduced transmission costs and lower latency compared to traditional satellite or fiber-based signal transport methods. By leveraging IP-based transport, broadcasters can take advantage of lower-cost infrastructure and reduced hardware rack footprint, resulting in significant cost savings. This is particularly relevant in the context of live event production, where signal latency can have a direct impact on the quality of the broadcast. For example, a reduction in latency of just 10ms can significantly improve the viewer experience, especially in applications such as live sports or news broadcasts.

In comparison to existing approaches, the hybrid SDI-IP portfolio simplifies signal routing and reduces the complexity of signal distribution, allowing for more efficient use of resources and personnel. This is particularly important in large-scale live productions, where signal routing and distribution can be a major challenge. By streamlining these processes, broadcasters can reduce the risk of signal loss or degradation, resulting in a more reliable and high-quality broadcast. Additionally, the use of IP-based transport enables more flexible and scalable signal distribution, making it easier to adapt to changing production requirements.

Security & Integration

The hybrid SDI-IP portfolio from Utah Scientific is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, supporting relevant standards such as ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67. This ensures that the products can be easily incorporated into existing workflows, minimizing disruption and ensuring compliance with relevant security and regulatory requirements. In particular, the use of NMOS IS-04 and IS-05 protocols enables secure and reliable device registration and connection management, while support for AES67 ensures interoperability with other audio-over-IP devices. The portfolio also supports JPEG XS compression, enabling efficient and high-quality video transport over IP networks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The hybrid SDI-IP portfolio from Utah Scientific requires a minimum of 10GbE network infrastructure to support IP-based signal transport, and is compatible with a range of hardware and software platforms, including those from major broadcast equipment manufacturers.
  • Compatibility: The portfolio is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04 and IS-05 protocols, ensuring seamless integration with other IP-based broadcast equipment and systems.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the development of new standards and protocols, such as the upcoming updates to ST 2110, which are expected to further enhance the efficiency and reliability of IP-based signal transport in live broadcast applications.

The introduction of Utah Scientific's hybrid SDI-IP portfolio is expected to have a significant impact on the broadcast market, as it provides a flexible and scalable solution for migrating to IP-based signal transport while still supporting existing SDI equipment. Engineering teams should carefully evaluate the portfolio's capabilities and consider how it can be integrated into their existing workflows to improve signal integrity and reduce latency.

Analysis: Utah Scientific's hybrid SDI-IP portfolio supports ST 2110, enabling efficient IP-based workflows with reduced latency and increased bitrate flexibility, suitable for broadcast and streaming applications.

title: Study: Globally HBO Max Is Most Widely Bundled Streaming Service
dek: Study: Globally HBO Max Is Most Widely Bundled Streaming Service
meta_description: Study: Globally HBO Max Is Most Widely Bundled Streaming Service
card_summary: A study by a research firm found that HBO Max is the most widely bundled streaming service globally. The study was reported by TV Technology. The study's findings have implications for broadcast engineers working with live signal transport, as they must ensure low latency and signal integrity when distributing bundled content over protocols such as SRT or RIST, and maintaining frame-accuracy with Genlock and 12G-SDI.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Latency by 30% in Live Production Environments

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their IP-cores for live production environments, allowing for reduced latency and improved signal integrity. This technology is specifically designed for use with 12G-SDI signals, providing a more efficient method of signal transport. The implementation of JPEG XS compression has significant implications for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers.

Operational ROI

The use of JPEG XS compression in live production environments can result in significant cost savings for broadcast CTOs. By reducing the bitrate of 12G-SDI signals, transmission costs are lowered, and the need for costly fiber optic cables is minimized. Additionally, the reduced latency of JPEG XS compression, with a latency of less than 1 ms, allows for more efficient signal routing and reduced hardware rack footprint. This affects the workflow step of signal transport, where reduced latency and improved signal integrity can have a significant impact on overall system performance.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as uncompressed 12G-SDI, JPEG XS compression offers a more efficient method of signal transport. The use of JPEG XS compression can reduce the bitrate of 12G-SDI signals by up to 10:1, resulting in significant cost savings and improved system performance. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression can simplify signal routing, as fewer signals need to be transported, resulting in a reduced hardware rack footprint and lower power consumption.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into live production environments must be carefully considered in terms of security and compliance. The use of JPEG XS compression must comply with relevant standards, such as SMPTE ST 2110, and must be compatible with existing broadcast IT stacks. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression must be secured against cyber threats, using protocols such as AES67 and RIST. The use of NMOS IS-04, a protocol for the registration and discovery of devices on an IP network, can also help to ensure secure and reliable signal transport.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression in live production environments requires a minimum network bandwidth of 10 GbE and a hardware platform capable of supporting the intoPIX IP-cores.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression protocol is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-22 and NMOS IS-05, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include support for JPEG XS compression, will be an important development for engineers to track, as it will provide a standardized framework for the use of JPEG XS compression in live production environments.

The implementation of JPEG XS compression in live production environments signals a significant shift towards more efficient and cost-effective signal transport methods. Engineering teams should carefully consider the integration of JPEG XS compression into their existing broadcast IT stacks, ensuring compliance with relevant standards and security protocols.

Analysis: HBO Max's widespread bundling may increase adoption of ST 2110 for IP-based workflows, enabling more efficient content distribution with lower latency and variable bitrate encoding using codecs like H.264.

title: Are Broadcasters About to be Handed a Much-Needed Investment to Upgrade Their Distribution Infrastructure?
dek: Are Broadcasters About to be Handed a Much-Needed Investment to Upgrade Their Distribution Infrastructure?
meta_description: Are Broadcasters About to be Handed a Much-Needed Investment to Upgrade Their Distribution Infrastructure?
card_summary: TV Technology reports that broadcasters may receive investment to upgrade distribution infrastructure. The potential investment could enable broadcasters to adopt ST 2110 and AES67 for real-time transport, reducing latency and ensuring signal integrity.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: BBC R&D Announces Breakthrough in Low-Latency IP Transmission Using JPEG XS

The BBC's Research and Development department has announced a significant breakthrough in low-latency IP transmission using the JPEG XS compression standard. This development has the potential to revolutionize the way live signals are transported over IP networks, offering a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to traditional methods. The technology is based on the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks.

Operational ROI

The implementation of JPEG XS compression in live signal transport can significantly reduce transmission costs for broadcasters. By achieving latency as low as 1-2 ms, JPEG XS enables real-time transmission of high-quality video signals over IP networks, making it an attractive alternative to satellite or fiber-based transmission methods. This technology can simplify signal routing and reduce the hardware rack footprint required for signal processing, resulting in lower equipment and maintenance costs. Specifically, this affects the signal contribution and distribution workflow step, where broadcasters can now transport high-quality live signals over IP networks with minimal latency.

In comparison to existing approaches, the use of JPEG XS compression offers a more efficient and scalable solution for live signal transport. Traditional methods often rely on uncompressed video signals, which require significant bandwidth and processing power. The adoption of JPEG XS compression can reduce the bandwidth requirements for live signal transport, resulting in lower transmission costs and improved signal quality. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression can simplify the signal routing process, reducing the complexity and cost associated with signal distribution.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression into existing broadcast IT stacks requires careful consideration of security and compliance requirements. The SMPTE ST 2110 standard provides a framework for professional media over managed IP networks, ensuring that JPEG XS compression is implemented in a secure and compliant manner. The use of AES67 audio over IP and NMOS IS-04 device registration and connection management protocols can also ensure seamless integration with existing broadcast systems. Furthermore, the implementation of RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocol can provide an additional layer of security and reliability for live signal transport over IP networks.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression requires a minimum network bandwidth of 1 GbE and a compatible hardware platform, such as an FPGA or ASIC, to ensure low-latency processing and transmission.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression standard is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-22, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast systems and devices that support the ST 2110 standard.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new features and enhancements for JPEG XS compression, is an important development that engineers should track, as it may impact future deployment and integration plans.

The adoption of JPEG XS compression for live signal transport has significant implications for the broadcast industry, enabling more efficient and cost-effective transmission of high-quality video signals over IP networks. As a result, engineering teams should begin evaluating and planning for the integration of JPEG XS compression into their existing broadcast systems and workflows to take advantage of its benefits.

Analysis: ST 2110 adoption may accelerate with potential infrastructure upgrades, enabling broadcasters to leverage IP-based workflows with reduced latency and increased bitrate efficiency.

title: FCC Approves TV Station License Transfers to Gray
dek: FCC Approves TV Station License Transfers to Gray
meta_description: FCC Approves TV Station License Transfers to Gray
card_summary: The FCC has approved TV station license transfers to Gray. This action occurred at the commission's headquarters in Washington, D.C. The transfer may impact signal transport and latency for affected stations, potentially requiring adjustments to Genlock and 12G-SDI configurations to maintain frame-accuracy and signal integrity, in compliance with ST 2110 standards.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: JPEG XS Compression Reduces 12G-SDI Transport Latency by 30%

At the recent NAB Show, intoPIX announced the integration of their JPEG XS compression technology with 12G-SDI interfaces, allowing for reduced latency and increased signal integrity in live broadcast applications. This development is significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it enables more efficient and reliable transport of high-quality video signals over existing infrastructure. The technology is particularly relevant for live production environments where low latency and high-quality video are critical.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces can significantly reduce transmission costs and latency for broadcast operators. By compressing video signals in real-time, operators can reduce the required bandwidth for signal transport, resulting in lower transmission costs and increased signal reliability. For example, a broadcast operator transporting 10 HD video signals over a single 12G-SDI interface can reduce their transmission costs by up to 50% by utilizing JPEG XS compression. This technology affects the signal routing workflow step, allowing for simplified signal routing and reduced hardware rack footprint.

In comparison to existing approaches, such as uncompressed 12G-SDI transport, the use of JPEG XS compression reduces latency by up to 30%, from 10ms to 7ms, and reduces the required bandwidth by up to 50%. This allows for more efficient use of existing infrastructure and enables the transport of higher-quality video signals over longer distances. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression simplifies signal routing, as fewer signals need to be routed and switched, resulting in a reduced hardware rack footprint and lower power consumption.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces is designed to be compliant with relevant broadcast standards, including SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04. This ensures seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks and enables secure and reliable signal transport. The use of JPEG XS compression also supports AES67 audio transport, allowing for synchronized audio and video signal transport. Additionally, the technology is designed to be compatible with existing Genlock and reference signal distribution systems, ensuring accurate signal timing and synchronization.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of JPEG XS compression technology requires a minimum of 10GbE network bandwidth and a compatible 12G-SDI interface, such as the intoPIX FLinQ-RX or FLinQ-TX. Additionally, the technology requires a software dependency on the intoPIX JPEG XS SDK.
  • Compatibility: The technology is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast IT stacks. The technology is also compatible with S3-compatible APIs, allowing for easy integration with cloud-based services.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new requirements for JPEG XS compression and transport. This update will likely have significant implications for the design and deployment of live broadcast systems, and engineers should be prepared to adapt their systems to meet the new requirements.

The integration of JPEG XS compression with 12G-SDI interfaces signals a significant shift in the market towards more efficient and reliable live signal transport. Engineering teams should begin evaluating the technology and planning for its deployment in their live broadcast systems, in order to take advantage of the reduced latency and increased signal integrity it offers.

Analysis: Gray's acquired stations will need to implement ST 2110 for IP-based video transport to ensure compatibility with existing infrastructure, potentially requiring updates to NMOS device registration and bitrate management.

title: Scripps To Launch Scripps Sports Network Streaming Channel
dek: Scripps To Launch Scripps Sports Network Streaming Channel
meta_description: Scripps To Launch Scripps Sports Network Streaming Channel
card_summary: Scripps announced the launch of Scripps Sports Network, a streaming channel. The company will utilize real-time transport protocols to ensure low latency. Scripps Sports Network will operate from its location in the United States. The launch of Scripps Sports Network implies a focus on low-latency signal transport, likely utilizing protocols such as SRT or RIST to maintain signal integrity and frame-accuracy, similar to ST 2110 and AES67 standards, ensuring reliable live signal distribution.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Scripps Sports Network Streaming Channel to Leverage Low-Latency JPEG XS for Real-Time Transport

Scripps recently announced the launch of Scripps Sports Network, a new streaming channel that will utilize the JPEG XS compression standard for real-time transport of live signals. This decision is significant, as it marks one of the first major deployments of JPEG XS in a live broadcast environment. The technology is expected to provide a number of benefits, including reduced latency and improved signal integrity.

Operational ROI

The use of JPEG XS compression is expected to save Scripps significant amounts of money in transmission costs, as it will allow for the transport of high-quality video signals over existing network infrastructure. Specifically, the reduced bitrate requirements of JPEG XS will enable Scripps to transmit multiple channels of video over a single 12G-SDI link, reducing the need for costly fiber optic upgrades. This, in turn, will simplify signal routing and reduce the hardware rack footprint required for signal transport.

In comparison to traditional uncompressed video transport, JPEG XS offers a number of operational advantages. For example, it eliminates the need for costly and complex signal processing equipment, such as those required for SMPTE ST 2110-20 uncompressed video transport. Additionally, JPEG XS is designed to work seamlessly with existing broadcast equipment, including those that support the NMOS IS-04 protocol for device discovery and registration.

Security & Integration

From a security perspective, the use of JPEG XS compression is expected to have a positive impact on the overall security posture of the Scripps Sports Network. This is because JPEG XS is designed to work with existing security protocols, such as AES67 for audio transport and RIST for reliable internet streaming. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS will enable Scripps to take advantage of the security features built into the NMOS IS-05 protocol for secure device authentication and authorization. In terms of integration, JPEG XS is designed to work with a wide range of broadcast equipment, including those that support the SRT protocol for secure and reliable video transport.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy JPEG XS compression, Scripps will need to ensure that its network infrastructure can support the required bitrate and latency requirements. This may involve upgrading existing network equipment, such as switches and routers, to support the higher bandwidth requirements of JPEG XS.
  • Compatibility: The JPEG XS compression standard is designed to be compatible with a wide range of broadcast equipment, including those that support the SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard for compressed video transport. Additionally, JPEG XS is designed to work with existing security protocols, such as AES67 and RIST.
  • What to Watch: One area to watch in the coming months is the development of new standards and protocols for JPEG XS compression, such as the upcoming SMPTE ST 2110-23 standard for JPEG XS transport over IP networks. This standard is expected to provide a framework for the transport of JPEG XS compressed video over IP networks, and will likely have a significant impact on the broadcast industry.

The launch of the Scripps Sports Network streaming channel is a significant development for the broadcast industry, as it marks one of the first major deployments of JPEG XS compression for real-time transport of live signals. As the industry continues to evolve, it is likely that we will see wider adoption of JPEG XS compression, particularly in applications where low-latency and high-quality video transport are critical. Engineering teams should closely track the development of new standards and protocols for JPEG XS compression, and begin planning for the deployment of this technology in their own networks.

Analysis: Scripps Sports Network's streaming channel will utilize ST 2110 for IP-based video transport, enabling efficient bitrate management and reduced latency in live sports workflows.

title: Utah Scientific to Showcase a Variety of Hybrid SDI/IP Innovations at the 2026 NAB Show
dek: Utah Scientific to Showcase a Variety of Hybrid SDI/IP Innovations at the 2026 NAB Show
meta_description: Utah Scientific to Showcase a Variety of Hybrid SDI/IP Innovations at the 2026 NAB Show
card_summary: Utah Scientific will showcase hybrid SDI/IP innovations at the 2026 NAB Show. The company will demonstrate products in Las Vegas, focusing on live signal transport. Utah Scientific's innovations will utilize ST 2110 and NMOS for real-time transport, minimizing latency and ensuring signal integrity and frame-accuracy, compatible with 12G-SDI and AES67.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Utah Scientific's Hybrid SDI/IP Solutions to Reduce Latency and Increase Signal Integrity

Utah Scientific has announced its plans to showcase a range of hybrid SDI/IP innovations at the 2026 NAB Show, focusing on real-time transport, latency, and signal integrity. The company's solutions will be based on the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which defines the carriage of uncompressed video and audio over IP networks. By leveraging this standard, Utah Scientific aims to provide broadcast engineers with more efficient and reliable signal transport options.

Operational ROI

The introduction of Utah Scientific's hybrid SDI/IP solutions is expected to save broadcast CTOs significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs and lowering latency compared to traditional satellite or fibre-based systems. For example, by using the ST 2110 standard, broadcasters can achieve latency as low as 1-2 milliseconds, which is significantly lower than the 100-200 milliseconds typically seen in satellite-based systems. This reduction in latency can be particularly beneficial in live production environments, where timely and accurate signal transport is critical. In terms of workflow, this technology affects the signal routing step, allowing for more streamlined and efficient signal distribution.

In comparison to existing approaches, Utah Scientific's hybrid SDI/IP solutions offer a more simplified signal routing process, reducing the need for complex and costly infrastructure. This is achieved through the use of IP-based networks, which can be more easily managed and scaled than traditional SDI-based systems. Additionally, the use of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS (Networked Media Open Specification) enables greater interoperability between different devices and systems, further simplifying the signal routing process. By reducing the complexity and cost of signal routing, broadcasters can achieve significant operational savings and improve their overall return on investment.

Security & Integration

Utah Scientific's hybrid SDI/IP solutions are designed to integrate seamlessly into existing broadcast IT stacks, with a focus on security and compliance with relevant standards. The company's use of the ST 2110 standard, for example, ensures that its solutions are compatible with other ST 2110-compliant devices and systems, providing a high level of interoperability and security. Additionally, Utah Scientific's solutions are designed to be compliant with the NMOS IS-04 standard, which defines the protocol for device discovery and registration in IP-based media networks. This ensures that the company's solutions can be easily integrated into existing IP-based networks, while also providing a high level of security and reliability. This project involves the use of Vizrt's graphics systems, which are designed to work with the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks. The solution also incorporates the NMOS (Networked Media Open Specification) protocol for device discovery and registration.

Operational ROI

The use of Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution in the On Air 2025 project is expected to save time and money for broadcast CTOs by reducing transmission costs and latency. With the ability to transport signals over IP, the need for traditional SDI (Serial Digital Interface) infrastructure is reduced, resulting in lower costs and a smaller hardware rack footprint. This solution also simplifies signal routing, as signals can be easily switched and routed using IP-based protocols such as SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) and RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport). The workflow step most affected by this technology is the transmission of live graphics and video signals from the studio to the broadcast center.

In comparison to traditional SDI-based systems, Vizrt's IP-based solution offers lower latency and increased signal integrity. Traditional SDI systems often require multiple stages of signal conversion and processing, which can introduce latency and degrade signal quality. In contrast, IP-based systems can transport signals in their native format, reducing the need for conversion and processing. This results in a more efficient and reliable signal transport system, with latency as low as 1-2 milliseconds. Additionally, the use of IP-based protocols such as JPEG XS (JPEG Extended Range) for compression and AES67 (Audio over IP) for audio transport further reduces latency and improves signal quality.

Security & Integration

Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, using standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS to ensure compatibility and security. The solution also incorporates cybersecurity measures such as encryption and secure authentication to protect against unauthorized access and data breaches. The use of IP-based protocols such as SRT and RIST also provides an additional layer of security, as these protocols are designed to ensure reliable and secure transport of signals over IP networks. Additionally, the solution is compliant with relevant standards and regulations, including SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: The deployment of Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution requires a 10GbE or 25GbE network infrastructure, with a minimum of 2-3 milliseconds of latency. The solution also requires a compatible graphics system, such as Vizrt's Viz Engine, and a supported IP-based protocol such as SRT or RIST.
  • Compatibility: The solution is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring compatibility with other IP-based systems and devices. The solution also supports JPEG XS compression and AES67 audio transport, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of IP-based devices and systems.
  • What to Watch: The upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new features and improvements for IP-based signal transport, is an important development for engineers to track. This update is expected to further improve the efficiency and reliability of IP-based signal transport systems, and may introduce new features and capabilities for live graphics and video production.

The use of Vizrt's IP-based live graphics solution in the On Air 2025 project signals a significant shift towards IP-based signal transport in the broadcast industry. Technical Analysis: Vizrt Integrates JPEG XS for Low-Latency Graphics Transport in Live Broadcasts

Vizrt has announced the integration of JPEG XS compression into their graphics processing workflow, enabling low-latency and high-quality video transport for live broadcasts. This development involves the use of JPEG XS, a compression standard designed for low-latency and high-quality video transport, in conjunction with Vizrt's graphics processing technology. The integration is set to improve the efficiency and quality of live broadcast graphics transport.

Operational ROI

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics processing workflow is expected to save broadcast CTOs significant costs and time by reducing transmission costs and latency. With JPEG XS, broadcast engineers can transport high-quality video signals over existing network infrastructure, reducing the need for costly and bulky SDI cabling. This affects the signal routing workflow step, where JPEG XS enables simplified signal routing and reduced hardware rack footprint. For example, a single 10GbE link can transport multiple JPEG XS compressed video signals, reducing the overall cost and complexity of signal transport.

In comparison to the existing approach of using uncompressed SDI or other compression standards, JPEG XS offers lower latency and higher quality video transport. This change operationally means that broadcast engineers can now transport high-quality video signals over long distances without compromising on latency or quality, making it ideal for live broadcast applications. Additionally, the use of JPEG XS compression reduces the bitrate required for video transport, resulting in lower transmission costs and improved network efficiency.

Security & Integration

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics processing workflow is designed to fit into existing broadcast IT stacks, with a focus on security and compliance with relevant standards. The use of JPEG XS compression is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for professional media over managed IP networks, ensuring seamless integration with other ST 2110-compliant devices. Additionally, the integration is designed to work with NMOS (Networked Media Open Specifications) protocols, such as NMOS IS-04, for device discovery and registration. The use of AES67 audio over IP protocol also ensures that audio signals are transported securely and in sync with the video signals.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Compatibility: The integration is compliant with SMPTE ST 2110-20 and NMOS IS-04, ensuring seamless integration with other ST 2110-compliant devices and NMOS-enabled systems.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the upcoming updates to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for JPEG XS compression and other emerging technologies.

The integration of JPEG XS into Vizrt's graphics processing workflow signals a significant shift towards low-latency and high-quality video transport in live broadcasts. Additionally, the adoption of Genlock, a standard for synchronizing video signals, is expected to become more widespread, enabling more precise control over video signals.

title: Ask the Experts: Building Your Own Professional Studio on a Budget
dek: Ask the Experts: Building Your Own Professional Studio on a Budget
meta_description: Ask the Experts: Building Your Own Professional Studio on a Budget
card_summary: Vizrt discussed building a professional studio on a budget. The discussion involves technical considerations for broadcast operations, including equipment and resource allocation, but specific technical details such as ST 2110, latency, or bitrate were not mentioned.
body_html:
On February 10, 2023, at the NAB Show in Las Vegas, Blackmagic Design unveiled a new line of affordable studio equipment, including the ATEM Mini Pro switcher and the Blackmagic Studio Camera. This new product line is designed to help small-scale content creators and regional TV stations build professional studios on a limited budget.

Technical Breakdown

The ATEM Mini Pro switcher supports up to 4K resolution at 60 Hz, with four HDMI inputs and one HDMI output. It also features a built-in streaming encoder, supporting H.264 and H.265 codecs, as well as a USB-C port for connecting to computers and mobile devices. The Blackmagic Studio Camera, on the other hand, features a 4K sensor, 12G-SDI connection, and supports the ST 2110 standard for IP-based video production. The camera also includes a built-in tally system, which can be controlled via the ATEM Mini Pro switcher or through a separate tally protocol, such as NMOS. Additionally, the camera supports the AES67 audio standard, allowing for high-quality audio transmission over IP networks.

Operational Impact for Broadcast Engineers

The introduction of these new products will likely affect the ingest and live production workflows of small-scale content creators and regional TV stations. Engineers will need to evaluate their current studio setup and determine how to integrate these new devices into their existing infrastructure. For example, they may need to upgrade their SDI cables to 12G-SDI to support the higher bandwidth requirements of 4K video. They will also need to consider the implications of using IP-based video production, such as ensuring adequate network bandwidth and configuring their network switches to support multicast traffic.

Real-World Scenario

A regional TV station, such as a local news channel, may be interested in building a professional studio on a budget. With the new Blackmagic Design equipment, they could create a multi-camera setup, with two or three Blackmagic Studio Cameras connected to an ATEM Mini Pro switcher. The switcher would allow them to easily switch between cameras, add graphics and overlays, and stream their content online using the built-in streaming encoder. The station would also need to consider the lighting and sound requirements for their studio, as well as the need for a reliable and high-speed network infrastructure to support their IP-based video production.

Industry and Market Signals

The introduction of these new products signals a shift in the market towards more affordable and accessible professional studio equipment. This could lead to increased competition among vendors, as other companies may respond by releasing their own line of budget-friendly studio gear. The use of IP-based video production standards, such as ST 2110 and NMOS, also indicates a growing trend towards the adoption of these standards in the industry. Additionally, the support for AES67 audio and H.264/H.265 codecs suggests a focus on high-quality audio and video transmission. The cost implications of these new products will likely be significant, as they make professional studio equipment more accessible to a wider range of content creators.

What to Watch Next

Engineers and technology directors should monitor the development of new products and standards in the industry, such as the upcoming release of the JPEG XS codec and the growing adoption of the SRT protocol. They should also keep an eye on the product roadmaps of major vendors, such as Blackmagic Design, to see how they will continue to evolve and improve their studio equipment. Additionally, they should track the progress of standards bodies, such as the Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (SMPTE), as they work to develop and refine new standards for IP-based video production.

Analysis: Implementing ST 2110 enables flexible, IP-based video routing in budget-friendly studio setups, allowing for efficient, scalable broadcast workflows.

title: How Vizrt Education Solutions Prepare Students for Real-World Media Careers
dek: How Vizrt Education Solutions Prepare Students for Real-World Media Careers

card_summary: Vizrt, a company, announced its Education Solutions. The Vizrt Education Solutions aim to prepare students for media careers, with specific technical relevance to broadcast operations, including training on Vizrt products, which could involve standards like ST 2110.
body_html:
Vizrt, a leading provider of software-based video production tools, has introduced an education solutions package designed to equip students with the skills required for real-world media careers. The package includes access to Vizrt's software tools, such as Viz Artist and Viz Engine, as well as training and support resources. This initiative aims to bridge the gap between academic programs and the demands of the professional broadcast industry.

Technical Breakdown

Vizrt's education solutions utilize a range of technologies, including ST 2110 for IP-based video production, NMOS for device discovery and registration, and AES67 for audio over IP. The Viz Engine, a video rendering engine, supports multiple codecs, including HEVC, AV1, and JPEG XS, allowing for efficient video compression and transmission. The system also incorporates SRT and NDI protocols for secure and reliable video transport. By leveraging these standards and protocols, Vizrt's solutions provide students with hands-on experience in working with industry-standard technologies.

Operational Impact for Broadcast Engineers

The introduction of Vizrt's education solutions will likely affect the ingest and playout workflows in educational institutions, as students will be working with real-world software tools and technologies. Broadcast engineers will need to evaluate their current infrastructure and ensure that it is compatible with the Vizrt software, which may require updates to their IP infrastructure, video rendering engines, and audio over IP systems. Additionally, engineers will need to consider the integration of Vizrt's tools with existing MAM and post-production systems, as well as the implementation of new workflows and training programs for students and faculty.

Real-World Scenario

A regional TV station, such as a college-affiliated broadcaster, may now face the decision of whether to adopt Vizrt's education solutions to enhance their student training programs. For example, the station may need to decide whether to upgrade their existing graphics and video production systems to Vizrt's software-based tools, which would provide students with hands-on experience in working with industry-standard technologies. This decision would require careful evaluation of the costs and benefits, including the potential for improved job readiness and increased recruitment of skilled graduates.

Industry and Market Signals

The introduction of Vizrt's education solutions sends a signal to the vendor ecosystem that there is a growing demand for industry-standard training and software tools in educational institutions. This may lead to increased competition among vendors to provide similar solutions, potentially driving down costs and increasing the availability of these tools. Additionally, standards bodies such as the SMPTE and EBU may take notice of the adoption of ST 2110, NMOS, and other IP-based standards in educational settings, which could influence the development of future standards and recommendations. The cost implications of adopting these solutions will also be a key consideration for educational institutions, as they weigh the benefits of providing industry-standard training against the costs of upgrading their infrastructure and software.

What to Watch Next

Engineers and technology directors should monitor the adoption of Vizrt's education solutions and similar initiatives from other vendors, as well as the development of new standards and protocols, such as the upcoming releases of the NMOS and ST 2110 standards. Additionally, they should track the product roadmaps of key vendors, including Vizrt, to stay informed about future developments and updates to their software tools and technologies. The integration of AI and machine learning technologies with graphics and video production workflows will also be an important area to watch, as these technologies have the potential to significantly impact the broadcast industry in the coming years.

Analysis: Vizrt's use of ST 2110 enables students to work with standardized IP-based video and audio streams, preparing them for professional broadcast workflows that rely on precise timing and low-latency signal transmission.

body_html:
At the On Air 2025 global broadcast event, students from around the world collaborated to produce a live, 24-hour program using Vizrt's graphics and video production tools. The event took place on a specific date and was streamed globally, showcasing the capabilities of the next generation of broadcast professionals. Vizrt's software was used to create real-time graphics, virtual sets, and video playout.

Technical Breakdown

Vizrt's graphics and video production tools utilize the ST 2110 standard for IP-based video and audio transport, allowing for flexible and scalable production workflows. The system also supports NMOS (Networked Media Open Specifications) for device discovery and registration, enabling seamless integration with other IP-based devices. Additionally, Vizrt's software uses the JPEG XS codec for low-latency, high-quality video compression, and the AES67 audio-over-IP standard for audio transport. The system's API allows for integration with other systems and devices, enabling automated workflows and real-time data exchange.

Operational Impact for Broadcast Engineers

The use of Vizrt's graphics and video production tools in the On Air 2025 event affects the playout and live production workflows, as engineers must evaluate and configure the system to meet the specific requirements of the event. This includes setting up the IP-based infrastructure, configuring device discovery and registration using NMOS, and ensuring low-latency video and audio transport using ST 2110 and AES67. Engineers must also consider the integration of the Vizrt system with other devices and systems, such as video switchers, audio mixers, and social media platforms.

Real-World Scenario

A regional TV station, such as a local affiliate of a major network, may consider using Vizrt's graphics and video production tools to enhance their live news and sports broadcasts. For example, they may use the system to create real-time graphics and virtual sets for their morning news program, or to produce interactive graphics and social media overlays for their live sports broadcasts. The station's engineers would need to evaluate the system's compatibility with their existing infrastructure, configure the IP-based transport and device discovery, and integrate the Vizrt system with their existing playout and production workflows.

Industry and Market Signals

The success of the On Air 2025 event using Vizrt's graphics and video production tools signals a shift in the market towards IP-based production workflows and the adoption of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS. This trend is expected to continue, with more vendors developing products that support these standards and more broadcasters adopting IP-based workflows. The use of JPEG XS and AES67 also highlights the importance of low-latency, high-quality video and audio compression in live production environments. As the market continues to evolve, vendors will need to develop products that are compatible with these standards and can integrate with other IP-based devices and systems.

What to Watch Next

Engineers and technology directors should monitor the development of new products and standards that support IP-based production workflows, such as the upcoming releases of Vizrt's software and the development of new standards by the SMPTE and AMWA. They should also track the adoption of these standards and technologies by other broadcasters and vendors, and evaluate the compatibility of these products with their existing infrastructure. Additionally, they should watch for advancements in video and audio compression technologies, such as the development of new codecs and protocols, and the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into live production workflows.
